newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada stock stages recovery after bid.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada stock stages recovery after bid.

text.p: Shares in Gulf Canada Resources Ltd rose in busy volume on Thursday as terms of the company's hostile takeover bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc sank in with investors.
Analysts said Gulf's surge in price was also attributed to a general rise in Canadian oil and gas stocks, which was fueled by continuing strong commodity prices.
Gulf Canada shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange gained C$0.60 to close Thursday's session at C$9.90, just C$0.10 below its 52-week high. Nearly 1.2 million shares changed hands.

Gulf on Wednesday said it planned to launch a C$972 million takeover bid for Clyde, a firm with producing assets in the North Sea and Australia, offering shareholders 105 pence in a debt-funded cash deal.

The Canadian firm said it would embark on asset sales, a public offering of 20 percent of its Indonesia subsidiary and an equity issue or setting of a royalty trust to repay its debt in 1997. Analysts and arbitrageurs on both sides of the Atlantic have said the jump in Clyde's share price following the announcement suggested strong odds of a rival bid surfacing.
Clyde shares in London closed on Thursday at 118 pence.
Wilf Gobert, analyst with Calgary-based Peters & Co Ltd said Gulf investors appeared to warm to the deal after driving its stock down on Wednesday.
"There have been a couple of days of trading now since the deal was announced. The stock's within a dime of its all-time high. The market seems to be reacting favorably," Gobert said.

However, Toronto's Oil & Gas Index climbed 97.25 points -- or 1.54 percent -- on Thursday to close at a strong 6,407.59 points as several Canadian energy producer stocks made large gains. "It was a pretty hot day in the market," Gobert said. ((-- Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
